mission: Watch the platform's own health — internal Vrooli code, lifecycle, autoheal/system-monitor history — and surface durable findings the operator can act on. Detect patterns across runtime incidents, audit internal code along the same dimensions scenario-qa applies to scenarios, and drive internal instrumentation forward so future findings are sharper.

instrument.gapMarker: 2026-08-20 (second revision) — the instrument is wired to its own condition domain and to a new substrate projection. Fixed since the first marker: the batch saturation read removed the N+1 per-check fan-out that was reporting deadline expiry as UNTRUSTED on roughly two thirds of checks; ghost classification now tests target existence rather than core-set membership, so installed scenarios outside the core set are reported as out-of-scope and stay in every aggregate; the focus surface now joins out-of-band and untrusted readings, so inner cascade tiers can outrank coverage gaps; and 24 of 28 setpoint bars now carry a unit and a numeric threshold, with the remaining four declared not-gradeable with stated reasons. Still open: substrate bars are provisional pending operator ratification, setpoint confidence is SKETCH, peer sources other than vrooli-autoheal have no typed reader, capability availability history is unavailable, the infra-health loop remains paused, and template provenance remains quarantined upstream. The plant remains the layer stack in docs/infra-health/operating/OPERATING_MODEL.md section Platform Under Control — not the *-health scenario fleet, which is scenario-qa's plant.

planOfRecord.rationale: Operating contract, cross-platform portability ledger, and editing authority. Reliability targets, sensor definitions and instrumentation gaps are NOT here — they are owned and computed by the infrastructure-manager instrument.
planOfRecord.useFor: team operating contract and routing rules, cross-platform portability ledger, and director-swarm morning-walk infrastructure work items

instrument.rationale: The team's instrument. Members read reliability state here instead of re-deriving it; no member may write to the setpoint, which is what stops the supervisor grading itself.
instrument.useFor: what to work next, whether a cell is in band, whether a reading can be believed, and which cells have no sensor at all

runtime-health-scanner.lane: Find aggregate runtime-health patterns across durable autoheal incidents, autoheal history, system-monitor, and lifecycle history; produce one concrete finding at a time.
safetyCriticalRules: Pick one signal per heartbeat; depth over breadth.
Never edit platform, autoheal, or system-monitor code.

taskParameters.triageLadder: SSOT is the Task Loop in members/runtime-health-scanner/HEARTBEAT.md — walk the ladder there in order (rounds 2-3 expanded it beyond the original five tiers). Do not maintain a second copy here.

platform-code-auditor.lane: Audit one slice of internal Vrooli platform code per heartbeat and route concrete findings through work items.
safetyCriticalRules: Never edit internal platform code directly.
Do not audit scenario code; scenario-qa owns that lane.

infra-contrarian.lane: Challenge infra-health work items against the team failure-mode rubric and run the stale work item scan. Also this team's shape sensor: hold the team against the target model's deviation catalogue and report deviations; never restructure.
safetyCriticalRules: Do not generate runtime or platform findings.
Do not edit code or plan-of-record docs.
Do not synthesize other members into a leader-style brief.

taskParameters.frameworkMetaCadence: at most one per calendar month
taskParameters.failureModes: SSOT is the Failure-Mode Rubric + Mechanical Thresholds in members/infra-contrarian/RESPONSIBILITIES.md — the operative set includes the mechanical fails (unit mismatch, dead-sensor, roster creep, cascade violation) added in rounds 2-3. Do not maintain a second copy here.
